question: What common operational problems occur with cyclones and multiclones?
answer: Common operational problems experienced with cyclones and multiclones include erosion of cyclone components that come into contact with high velocity particles; plugging of the dust outlet or the gas inlet vanes; corrosion from contact with acid gases in the inlet gas stream; and air inleakage that affects the inlet velocity and control efficiency of the cyclone. question: What is roping in a cyclone and why is it undesirable?
answer: Roping in a cyclone occurs when the spigot is choked, meaning it is discharging its maximum amount of solids, and any coarse solids that cannot get out of the spigot are forced into the wrong direction, out the cyclone overflow. [1] This is undesirable because it reduces the efficiency of the cyclone, as the greater the water content in the underflow, the more bypassing of fines occurs in the cyclone. [1]

[3] Check for any signs of wear or damage to the filters. [3]
